ECE 6390

Hard decisions and soft reliability

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows how a log-likelihood ratio keeps information that a hard zero-or-one decision discards.

A hard decision keeps a bit label. A soft observation also records how strongly the sample supports that label under the channel model. A small positive sample and a large positive sample both produce bit 1 at a zero threshold, but their error evidence differs.

For Gaussian observations with means ±A, common variance σ² and bit 1 assigned to +A, the natural-log likelihood ratio is L(y) = ln[p(y|1)/p(y|0)] = 2Ay/σ². Positive L favors 1 and negative L favors 0. The ratio is dimensionless; its magnitude depends on the noise scale as well as the observed amplitude.

With prior probability p₁, posterior log odds are Lpost = L(y)+ln(p₁/(1−p₁)). A posterior error probability for the selected bit is 1/(1+exp(|Lpost|)) under this model. The adjustable figure separates channel evidence from prior evidence so the effect of each remains visible.

Soft code decoders combine these observations with code constraints. Some software uses the reverse likelihood ratio and sign convention, which must be translated explicitly. Confidence computed under an incorrect channel model can be misleading; the number is not an unconditional physical guarantee.

Example

At A = 1, σ = 0.5 and y = 0.1, L = 0.8. With equal priors, the posterior chance of bit 1 is about 0.690. At y = 1.2 with the same noise, L = 9.6 and that probability is about 0.99993. Both samples yield the same hard bit.

Practice

1. If σ doubles while A and y stay fixed, how does the channel LLR change?

Its denominator is the noise variance.

It falls to one quarter becauseσ² grows by four. The same observation is weaker evidence under a noisier model.

2. Does an LLR of 0 mean a measured zero voltage in every receiver?

Separate the likelihood ratio from prior odds and the chosen signal model.

Here channel LLR 0 occurs at y 0, but posterior log odds can be nonzero because of unequal priors. A different observation model or sign convention also changes how sample values map to evidence.
